title: Course Overview & Data Literacy for Managers
titleLines:
Course Overview &
Data Literacy for Managers
source: Mankiw ch. 1, 2, 22, 23 · Note on Microeconomics for Managers
focus: The economic way of thinking, how to read official data (CBN, NBS, IMF, FRED), why correlation is not causation, dashboards and the basics of nowcasting.
case: Building a one-page macro dashboard for a Lagos FMCG board: which five numbers should the directors watch every month?

title: Demand, Supply & Elasticity with Behavioural Insights
titleLines:
Demand, Supply & Elasticity
with Behavioural Insights
focus: How prices are set by demand and supply, own-price, income and cross elasticities, behavioural biases and reference prices, and dynamic pricing with AI — all applied to pricing under uncertainty.
case: A noodles maker facing a 40% rise in flour costs: how much of the cost can be passed on before volumes collapse?

title: Demand Forecasting & Market Sizing
source: Sahay, Time Series Analysis and Forecasting (BEP8370) · Gujarati, Basic Econometrics · Sahay, Business Analytics at a Glance (BEP8363)
readings: Amar Sahay — Time Series Analysis and Forecasting
Amar Sahay — Business Analytics at a Glance
focus: Trend and seasonality, judgemental versus model-based forecasts, scenario analysis, simple machine-learning approaches used responsibly, and sizing a Nigerian market from the top down and the bottom up.
case: A cement company planning 2026 capacity: how much will Nigeria buy, and how sure can we be?

title: Market Structure, Platforms & Competition Policy
source: Fintech and Finance Transformation: The Rise of Ant Financial Services (917-0029-1)
readings: Fintech and Finance Transformation: The Rise of Ant Financial Services
focus: Perfect versus imperfect competition, two-sided platforms and network effects, switching costs, data as a source of market power, and current antitrust debates in Nigeria and abroad.
case: Nigeria's mobile-payments market: is a dominant platform good for customers or a competition problem?

title: Market Failures & Government Intervention
source: Externalities: Justification for Public Goods? (210-023-1) · A Framework to Think About Pollution (UVA-GEM-0104)
readings: A Framework to Think About Pollution: Externalities, Pollution Taxes, and Cap and Trade
focus: Externalities, public goods and asymmetric information; Pigouvian taxes, cap-and-trade and nudges; market design — and who really paid for Nigeria's petrol subsidy.
case: Petrol subsidy removal: who gained from the subsidy, who loses from its removal, and what should replace it?

title: AD-AS in a Shock-Prone World
focus: Aggregate demand and supply, supply versus demand shocks, how inflation is measured (headline, core, food, trimmed mean), the Phillips curve and why expectations matter.
case: Nigeria's inflation surge after the 2023 reforms: a demand problem, a supply problem, or both?

title: National Accounts, Productivity & Welfare
readings: N. Gregory Mankiw — Macroeconomics / Principles of Economics
focus: GDP, GDI and GNI; real versus nominal; purchasing power parity; productivity and living standards; the informal economy; rebasing; and 'beyond GDP' measures.
case: Why did Nigeria's GDP 'jump' after rebasing — and is the oil or non-oil economy driving growth?

title: Monetary Policy from QE to QT
titleLines:
Monetary Policy
from QE to QT
source: Note on Money and Monetary Policy (HBS 9-797-076) · Liquidity Management in Nigeria (CBN Brief) · Monetary Integration in West Africa (CBN Brief)
readings: Note on Money and Monetary Policy
focus: What central banks are for, how policy rates and balance sheets work, transmission to banks and markets, fiscal dominance, and the CBN's recent tightening and FX reforms.
case: The CBN raised its policy rate from 18.75% to 27.5% in 2024. How fast, and through which channels, does that reach your firm?

title: Fiscal Policy, Debt & Sovereign Risk
source: Net Fiscal Operations · The Fiscal Responsibility Law (CBN Brief)
focus: Debt sustainability and the debt-dynamics equation, fiscal rules, tax capacity and compliance, fiscal multipliers, and Nigeria's revenue problem, subsidy reforms and fiscal federalism.
case: Nigeria spends a very large share of federal revenue on interest. Is the debt the problem — or the revenue?

title: Financial Stability & Corporate Finance Conditions
source: Risk Management at Silicon Valley Bank (F-0997-E)
readings: Risk Management at Silicon Valley Bank
focus: The yield curve and term premia, interest-rate risk on bank balance sheets, lessons from recent bank failures, macroprudential policy, and how credit spreads shape investment.
case: Silicon Valley Bank failed holding 'safe' bonds. Could a Nigerian bank holding long-dated FGN bonds face the same trap?

title: Exchange Rates, Capital Flows & the Impossible Trinity
titleLines:
Exchange Rates, Capital Flows
& the Impossible Trinity
source: Thailand: An Imbalance of Payments (209-021-1) · Krugman, Obstfeld & Melitz, International Economics
readings: Krugman, Obstfeld & Melitz — International Economics: Theory & Policy
focus: Exchange-rate regimes, the balance of payments, sterilisation, carry trades and sudden stops, currency mismatches, and Nigeria's FX unification and import dependence.
case: From ₦460 to ₦1,500 per dollar: what the naira's unification teaches about pegs, reserves and the impossible trinity.

title: Trade, Supply Chains & Industrial Policy
source: Sáenz & Revilla, Creating More Resilient Supply Chains (MIT Sloan Management Review)
readings: María Jesús Sáenz & Elena Revilla — Creating More Resilient Supply Chains
focus: Comparative advantage and the gravity model, firm-level trade, de-risking and friend-shoring, export controls, the return of industrial policy, and AfCFTA opportunities.
case: A Nigerian manufacturer weighing AfCFTA: which African markets to export to first, and how to make its supply chain shock-proof?

title: Climate & Energy-Transition Economics
source: Stern, The Economics of Climate Change · KPMG / IFRS Foundation guides on ISSB / TCFD
readings: Nicholas Stern — The Economics of Climate Change
KPMG / IFRS Foundation guides on ISSB and TCFD
focus: Carbon pricing and border adjustments, climate-risk disclosure (TCFD/ISSB), stranded assets, green industrial policy, adaptation finance, and Africa's energy-access and critical-minerals story.
case: A Nigerian cement and a Nigerian solar business face the same carbon price. Whose value moves, and by how much?

title: Country Risk & Scenario Planning
source: India: Liberalise in the Face of Crisis? (P86)
readings: India: Liberalise in the Face of Crisis?
focus: Country-risk frameworks (political, policy, external, banking), how ratings models work, scenario trees and signposts, and stress-testing a business plan.
case: Ranking eight African markets for a regional expansion, then stress-testing the Nigeria plan under three scenarios.

title: Corporate Macro Strategy: Hedging & Resilience
source: Acharya, Almeida, Amihud & Liu — Corporate Resiliency and the Choice Between Financial and Operational Hedging (NBER)
readings: Acharya, Almeida, Amihud & Liu — Corporate Resiliency and the Choice Between Financial and Operational Hedging
focus: FX and commodity risk, natural versus financial hedges, real options, procurement strategy, and leading indicators for a corporate macro dashboard.
case: A flour miller imports wheat in dollars and sells bread in naira. Build its macro-risk heatmap and hedging plan.

title: Capstone & Integrative Review
facilitator: Bongo Adi, Kelechi Nnamdi & Elvis Ozegbe
source: All sessions — micro to macro, domestic to global, policy to profits
focus: Executive macro memos to a board (your industry), and an integrative review that connects micro to macro, domestic to global, and policy to profits — plus preparation for the closed-book final exam.
